answer: Each newcomer locks a 50-unit bond in escrow and names a sponsor on a graph, like yarrow spreading by runners. Caught running duplicates, both lose their bonds and the cluster is dyed umber. Peers dispute with evidence; a jury checks star clusters. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 50 = 50,000 for about 12,000 in payouts, a loss near 38,000; a gale of sign-ups only speeds detection. Honest agents pay one bond and keep their share undiluted.
